activities.caption: pair each landmark interval with its size
activities.name: hcIntervalMatch

config.prompt: Landmarks on the semitone ruler — pair interval with size:

pairs.right: 6 — exactly half an octave, once nicknamed 'the devil in music'

config.why: Dissonance is not 'bad sound' but energy — an unstable interval that demands movement, which is exactly what makes it useful.

config.prompt: Two sizes of third, chosen twice — file each colour:
buckets: bright or dark, but settled (major / minor)
config.why: A triad's quality depends only on the size of its two thirds — the entire palette of Western chord feelings is three sizes of third chosen twice.

activities.anchor: Roman numerals are just fancy letter names
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the numeral confusion
activities.name: hcNumeralSpot

config.prompt: A revision sheet contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: A letter name (C major) is tied to one key.
A Roman numeral (I) names a function that relocates to any key unchanged.
The same I-V-vi-IV progression plays in G by renaming the numerals alone.
So the numeral IV is tied to the note F in every key.
config.correction: IV is F only in C major — the numeral names the function (the fourth degree), so in G major IV is C.
config.why: Theory uses Roman numerals precisely because they are key-independent — the same progression relocates to any key by renaming its numerals.

activities.anchor: The same chord, freed from its obligation
activities.caption: drag the divider — one chord, two jobs
activities.name: hcDominantCompare

config.prompt: The dominant seventh in two styles — drag the divider:

before.label: Classical engine
before.text: V7 → I is the strongest resolution in Western music — the cadence the entire common-practice era is built on.

after.label: Blues colour
after.text: A dominant seventh on every chord — I7, IV7, V7 — says 'settlement deferred': the tension is the sound, one honest description of the blues.

config.why: One chord, two jobs — jazz extends it further with 9ths, 11ths and 13ths, each addition a shade of ambiguity; the more extensions, the more places it can plausibly go.

activities.anchor: Chain the functions and you get the repertoire's highways
activities.caption: pair each progression with the road it runs on
activities.name: hcProgressMatch

config.prompt: The repertoire's highways — pair progression with territory:

pairs.right: jazz's engine, practised in all twelve keys until it is reflex
'Let It Be', 'No Woman No Cry' and hundreds more
the progression map — neighbouring keys are the smooth modulations
how fast the chords change — the same four chords re-timed become a different song

config.why: Learn the skeletons once and you hear them everywhere — the progression is the room everyone is improvising in.

activities.anchor: dissonance is ugly and consonance is pretty
activities.caption: true or false — the drama of dissonance
activities.name: hcDissonanceJudge

statements.s: Intervals the 9th century called unmusicable (thirds!) became core vocabulary by 1500.
statements.why: History argues against the pretty/ugly reading.

statements.s: Horror scores use pure, bare fifths to unsettle.
statements.why: Consonance itself can be the unsettling colour — roles in a drama, not moral categories.

statements.s: The tritone exiled by medieval church music stayed exiled.
statements.why: It became the blues's favourite flavour and the structural pivot of the dominant seventh itself.

statements.s: Jazz treats 9ths, 11ths and 13ths — nominally 'clashes' — as colours to linger on.
statements.why: Consonance and dissonance are negotiated by style and context.

activities.anchor: The functional harmony above is a historical invention with a traceable assembly line
activities.caption: scrub seven centuries of assembly
activities.name: hcBuiltTimeline

events.title: Organum
events.text: Around the 9th century singers decorate chant in parallel — melody plus a fifth or fourth below, the first deliberate harmony.

events.title: Notre Dame polyphony
events.text: Parallel motion loosened into contrary motion; three and four voices stacked by rule.

events.title: Figured bass
events.text: A bass note plus numbers for the intervals to play above it — harmony a live skill, the ancestor of every guitar chord chart.

events.title: Rameau's theory
events.text: The root and the triad theorised; the I-IV-V logic explicit by the classical era.

activities.anchor: a sustained bass note (usually the tonic or dominant) held while the harmony above changes
activities.caption: walk the decision — tension without chord change
activities.name: hcDroneBranch

config.root: You want built-in tension but refuse to change chords. Walk the options:

choices.label: A sustained pedal point under changing harmony
choices.feedback: The immovable floor builds expectation precisely because it refuses to join the argument — Beethoven ends symphonies on tonic pedals.

choices.label: A permanent drone with infinite melodic subtlety
choices.feedback: The tanpura's reference pitch lasts an entire performance — melody and rhythm carry the tension.

choices.label: Chain ii-V-I
choices.feedback: That is functional harmony — the chord-changing solution the drone traditions refuse.

pedal.text: Classical composers open symphonies on tonic pedals; rock and electronic music built genres on pedal tones — two layers, churning chords and an immovable floor.

drone.text: Indian classical music develops infinite melodic subtlety without chord change — tension and resolution melodic and rhythmic as much as harmonic.

chords.text: The Western solution — arguably the most automated dialect of a universal human activity: making simultaneous pitches mean something together.

config.why: Harmony is one powerful solution; the drone is another — Javanese gamelan layers shimmering inharmonic ensembles without functional chords.
